description: Semantic companion to the GQL schema migrations. GQL defines structure; this file defines semantics not expressible in GQL: labels, descriptions, usage notes, examples, domain/range constraints, OWL-style edge qualifiers (transitive/symmetric/inverse_of), canonical storage direction, and MaRDI cross-references. Consumers: extraction/graph-update prompt injection, schema linting, user-facing help, future RDF/OWL export. See docs/mardi/PLAN-mardi-schema-alignment.md.
storage_convention: Lean storage (MathModDB convention): for inverse pairs only the canonical direction is stored; the inverse is expanded at query time. Symmetric edges are stored once, in either direction. Transitive edges store only direct links; closure is computed at query time.

Document.label: document
Document.description: A document tracked by the KB: an ingested raw paper/report or a synthesized overview. Anchor for provenance — nearly every other node cites Document ids in its sources.
Document.usage: Created by the ingest pipeline; do not create domain content without a Document source.

Author.label: author
Author.description: A person (or group) credited as author of a Document.

Venue.label: venue
Venue.description: Publication venue (journal, conference, workshop) of a Document.

Concept.label: concept
Concept.description: A general domain concept that is not (yet) a more specific type. Use sparingly — prefer specific types (Model, Algorithm, Quantity, ...) when applicable.

Method.label: method
Method.description: A methodological approach or procedure, broader/looser than an Algorithm. Kept distinct from Algorithm for now (may later merge into the Algorithm subclass hierarchy).

Algorithm.label: algorithm
Algorithm.description: A sequence of operations that solves a ComputationalTask. Organized in transitive SUBCLASS_OF hierarchies and HAS_COMPONENT decompositions; symmetric RELATED_TO links share algorithmic ideas.

Model.label: mathematical model
Model.description: A mathematical model: an abstract formalization of an ApplicationProblem, containing Equations and Quantities, and linked to the ComputationalTasks it is used by.
Model.usage: Central anchor on the model side. Prefer linking models to algorithms indirectly via ComputationalTask (USED_BY/SOLVES) rather than direct Model-Algorithm edges.

Equation.label: equation / formula
Equation.description: A mathematical formulation (formula, equation, constraint) with an optional LaTeX rendering. MaRDI 'formula'. Assumptions should be expressed as Equations and linked via ASSUMES.

extra_properties.latex: LaTeX source of the defining formula

Quantity.label: quantity
Quantity.description: A concrete quantity appearing in equations (has symbol and optionally unit). Specializes a QuantityKind.

QuantityKind.label: quantity kind
QuantityKind.description: An abstract quantity type (e.g. length, time, mass) independent of any particular model. Anchor for QUDT/ISQ alignment.

Assumption.label: assumption
Assumption.description: An assumption under which a Model, Equation, or ComputationalTask holds, expressed informally (natural language) when no formal statement exists or the document does not provide one. When an assumption IS expressed equationally in the source, prefer capturing it as an Equation and linking it via ASSUMES (MaRDI convention). Both forms are valid ASSUMES targets; choose per document fidelity.
Assumption.usage: Capture assumptions as they appear in the document — do not formalize beyond what the source states.

Metric.label: metric
Metric.description: An evaluation metric used to assess algorithms, estimators, or systems.

Dataset.label: dataset
Dataset.description: A collection of data used for evaluation or training. Distinct from Benchmark: a Dataset is raw material; a Benchmark is a standardized task instance.

Benchmark.label: benchmark
Benchmark.description: A standardized instance of a ComputationalTask used to test, evaluate and compare algorithms and software.

Tool.label: software / tool
Tool.description: A software package or tool implementing algorithms or used in experiments. MaRDI 'software'.

Application.label: application
Application.description: DEPRECATED in favor of ApplicationProblem. Existing nodes are retyped by the 0005 data migration.

ApplicationProblem.label: application problem
ApplicationProblem.description: A practical or scientific problem to be solved with the help of mathematical models (paper-era MaRDI 'Application Problem'; deliberately NOT restricted to research).
ApplicationProblem.usage: Contained in an ApplicationDomain; MODELLED_BY one or more Models.

ApplicationDomain.label: application domain
ApplicationDomain.description: A domain in which application problems arise (e.g. robotics, civil engineering, epidemiology). Lightweight anchor for external subject classifications (MSC, PhysSH, ANZSRC) via properties rather than a managed taxonomy.

ComputationalTask.label: computational task
ComputationalTask.description: A well-posed mathematical/computational task derived from a model (simulation, inversion, state estimation, parameter identification, optimization, ...). The bridge between models and algorithms: Model USED_BY task, Algorithm SOLVES task, Benchmark INSTANCE_OF task.
ComputationalTask.usage: Link models to algorithms through this node, never directly, so new algorithms become available to all models sharing the task.

System.label: system
System.description: An engineered or physical system under study (e.g. a robot platform, a sensor rig).

FactorGraph.label: factor graph
FactorGraph.description: A factor graph: bipartite probabilistic graphical model of Variables and Factors, typically optimized by a StateEstimator.

Variable.label: variable
Variable.description: A state variable in a factor graph or estimation problem.

Factor.label: factor
Factor.description: A factor in a factor graph: a probabilistic constraint over variables, derived from a measurement or prior.

StateEstimator.label: state estimator
StateEstimator.description: A system/algorithm configuration that estimates state variables from measurements (e.g. EKF, factor-graph smoother).

MotionModel.label: motion model
MotionModel.description: A process model predicting state evolution over time, used by estimators.

SensorModel.label: sensor model
SensorModel.description: A measurement model mapping state (and sensor parameters) to expected observations.

extra_properties.modality: e.g. camera, IMU, lidar, wheel odometry

Solver.label: solver
Solver.description: A numerical solver/optimizer (e.g. Levenberg-Marquardt, IPOPT) used inside algorithms or estimators.

Constraint.label: constraint
Constraint.description: A constraint restricting admissible states, parameters, or solutions.

CoordinateFrame.label: coordinate frame
CoordinateFrame.description: A named coordinate frame and its convention (e.g. body frame, ENU, camera optical frame).

Robot.label: robot
Robot.description: A robot platform or robot type under study.

Task.label: task
Task.description: A robot/system-level task (e.g. navigation, mapping). Distinct from ComputationalTask, which is the mathematical task derived from a model. Computational Task-nodes are migrated to ComputationalTask by the 0005 data migration.

NoiseModel.label: noise model
NoiseModel.description: A stochastic model of measurement or process noise.

Claim.label: claim
Claim.description: A reified statement: subject (via ABOUT), predicate, and object (via HAS_OBJECT to an entity, or object_literal). Used for facts that need qualifiers or provenance beyond a plain edge.

extra_properties.object_literal: literal object if not an entity

Acronym.label: acronym
Acronym.description: An acronym/abbreviation and its expansion, for domain-agnostic term resolution.

AUTHORED_BY.label: authored by
AUTHORED_BY.description: Document is authored by an Author.

PUBLISHED_IN.label: published in
PUBLISHED_IN.description: Document was published in a Venue.

DERIVED_FROM.label: derived from
DERIVED_FROM.description: Entity (typically a synthesized Document or a refined node) is derived from another entity.

MENTIONS.label: mentions
MENTIONS.description: Document mentions an entity (weak link; prefer typed relations when the role is known).

DEFINES.label: defines
DEFINES.description: Document formally defines an entity (stronger than MENTIONS).

SUPPORTS.label: supports
SUPPORTS.description: Document or Claim provides evidence supporting another Document or Claim.

CONTRADICTS.label: contradicts
CONTRADICTS.description: Document or Claim contradicts another Document or Claim.

RELATES_TO.label: relates to
RELATES_TO.description: Generic association when no more specific relation applies. Prefer typed relations.

PART_OF.label: part of
PART_OF.description: Structural containment/composition between entities of any kind (component —PART_OF→ whole).

SPECIALIZES.label: specializes
SPECIALIZES.description: A is a specialization/constraint/special case of B, within the same node type. Used for Model, Equation, Quantity, ComputationalTask, ApplicationProblem, ApplicationDomain, Algorithm hierarchies.
SPECIALIZES.usage: Store only direct specialization links; query helpers compute the transitive closure.
SPECIALIZES.mardi_source: MathModDB P1684 'specialized by' (we store the inverse direction); MathAlgoDB :specializes

USES.label: uses
USES.description: Entity employs another entity as a tool/component/ingredient. For algorithms prefer HAS_COMPONENT; for the model→task bridge use USED_BY.

IMPLEMENTS.label: implements
IMPLEMENTS.description: Tool (software), Algorithm, or System implements a Method or Algorithm.

APPLIES_TO.label: applies to
APPLIES_TO.description: Entity applies to / is relevant for another entity (e.g. method applies to a problem class). Where an ApplicationProblem is modelled by a Model, prefer MODELLED_BY.

HAS_VARIABLE.label: has variable
HAS_VARIABLE.description: FactorGraph or Factor involves a Variable.

CONNECTS.label: connects
CONNECTS.description: Factor connects to a Variable (factor-graph incidence).

ESTIMATES.label: estimates
ESTIMATES.description: StateEstimator estimates a Variable or Quantity.

MEASURES.label: measures
MEASURES.description: Sensor or SensorModel measures a Quantity or Variable.

ASSUMES.label: assumes
ASSUMES.description: Model, Equation, or ComputationalTask holds under the assumption expressed by the target. The target is an Equation when the assumption is stated formally, or an Assumption node for informal/natural-language assumptions — both are first-class.
ASSUMES.usage: Match the document's level of formalization: Equation target for stated formulas, Assumption node otherwise.

OPTIMIZES.label: optimizes
OPTIMIZES.description: Solver or StateEstimator optimizes a FactorGraph or objective.

SOLVED_BY.label: solved by
SOLVED_BY.description: Legacy/general 'is solved by' link. For the model/algorithm alignment prefer ComputationalTask + SOLVES.

DEFINED_BY.label: defined by
DEFINED_BY.description: Entity is formally defined by an Equation (e.g. Algorithm DEFINED_BY Equation, Variable DEFINED_BY Equation). For Quantity, DEFINED_BY is an optional refinement on top of the mandatory EXPRESSED_BY edge to designate canonical / axiomatic definitions.

EVALUATED_ON.label: evaluated on
EVALUATED_ON.description: Algorithm/Tool is evaluated on a Dataset or Benchmark; Metric may be involved via Claims.

EXPRESSED_IN.label: expressed in
EXPRESSED_IN.description: Quantity or Equation is expressed in a CoordinateFrame or unit context.

HAS_NOISE.label: has noise model
HAS_NOISE.description: SensorModel or MotionModel has a NoiseModel.

USES_SYMBOL.label: uses symbol
USES_SYMBOL.description: Equation, MotionModel, or Method uses a Quantity/Variable as a symbol in its mathematical expression (MaRDI 'in defining formula', P983).

EXPRESSED_BY.label: expressed by
EXPRESSED_BY.description: Model, MotionModel, SensorModel, NoiseModel, Algorithm, Method, ComputationalTask, or Quantity is expressed by an Equation or MotionModel (its mathematical formulation). For Quantity, EXPRESSED_BY is the mandatory structural relationship connecting an isolated/defined LHS output quantity to its defining Equation.

USES_ACRONYM.label: uses acronym
USES_ACRONYM.description: Entity (Document, Method, Algorithm, Equation, Model, Robot, etc.) uses an Acronym in its text or definition.

STANDS_FOR.label: stands for
STANDS_FOR.description: Acronym stands for an entity it abbreviates.

MODELLED_BY.label: modelled by
MODELLED_BY.description: An ApplicationProblem P is modelled by a Model M if M formalizes P so it can be treated with mathematical/numerical methods.
MODELLED_BY.usage: Canonical direction of the pair (MathModDB lean convention). The inverse MODELS is expanded at query time.
MODELLED_BY.example: microfracture detection in porous media —MODELLED_BY→ X-ray transform model

MODELS.label: models
MODELS.description: Inverse of MODELLED_BY: a Model formalizes an ApplicationProblem. Not stored; expanded at query time.

USED_BY.label: used by
USED_BY.description: A Model is used by a ComputationalTask: the mathematical task that must be solved to apply the model. The MathModDB→MathAlgoDB bridge.
USED_BY.usage: Canonical bridge edge. Algorithms reach the model indirectly via SOLVES on the same task.
USED_BY.example: X-ray transform model —USED_BY→ inversion of the X-ray transform

SOLVES.label: solves
SOLVES.description: An Algorithm, Method, or StateEstimator provides a solution to a ComputationalTask.

INSTANCE_OF.label: instance of
INSTANCE_OF.description: A Benchmark is a concrete, standardized instance of a ComputationalTask.

TESTS.label: tests
TESTS.description: A Tool (software) is run against a Benchmark.

SUBCLASS_OF.label: subclass of (algorithm)
SUBCLASS_OF.description: Algorithm A is a subclass of algorithm B if B is the simpler/more general version and A uses the essential algorithmic ideas of B (e.g. EKF SUBCLASS_OF KF).
SUBCLASS_OF.usage: Store only direct links; transitive closure at query time.

HAS_COMPONENT.label: has component
HAS_COMPONENT.description: Algorithm A has component algorithm B if B is used to complete A (e.g. a smoother HAS_COMPONENT a linear solver).

DISCRETIZED_BY.label: discretized by
DISCRETIZED_BY.description: A continuous Model/Equation is discretized by another Model/Equation (e.g. Hamiltonian operator —DISCRETIZED_BY→ discrete Hamiltonian).

LINEARIZED_BY.label: linearized by
LINEARIZED_BY.description: A nonlinear Model/Equation/ComputationalTask is linearized by another (e.g. nonlinear motion model —LINEARIZED_BY→ its Jacobian linearization).

APPROXIMATED_BY.label: approximated by
APPROXIMATED_BY.description: A Model/Equation is approximated by a simpler or reduced Model/Equation (e.g. full model —APPROXIMATED_BY→ reduced-order model).

NONDIMENSIONALIZED_BY.label: nondimensionalized by
NONDIMENSIONALIZED_BY.description: A Quantity is nondimensionalized by another Quantity (e.g. permittivity —NONDIMENSIONALIZED_BY→ relative permittivity).

HAS_WEAK_FORMULATION.label: has weak formulation
HAS_WEAK_FORMULATION.description: An Equation or Model (strong form) has the target Equation or Model as its weak/variational formulation.

SOLUTION_TO.label: solution to
SOLUTION_TO.description: An Equation is a (known analytical) solution to a Model.

SIMILAR_TO.label: similar to
SIMILAR_TO.description: Two entities of the same type are similar but neither is a specialization/generalization of the other.
SIMILAR_TO.usage: Store once, in either direction; matched both ways at query time.

INVENTED_IN.label: invented in
INVENTED_IN.description: Algorithm was invented/introduced in a Document (publication). Multiple documents may invent the same algorithm.

ANALYZED_IN.label: analyzed in
ANALYZED_IN.description: Algorithm's theoretical analysis appears in a Document.

STUDIED_IN.label: studied in
STUDIED_IN.description: Algorithm is numerically tested/studied in a Document.

APPLIED_IN.label: applied in
APPLIED_IN.description: Algorithm is practically applied in a Document.

REVIEWED_IN.label: reviewed in
REVIEWED_IN.description: Algorithm is described in a survey/review Document.

DOCUMENTED_IN.label: documented in
DOCUMENTED_IN.description: Tool or Benchmark is described in a Document.

USED_IN.label: used in
USED_IN.description: Tool or Benchmark is utilized for computer-based experiments in a Document.

HAS_KIND.label: has quantity kind
HAS_KIND.description: A Quantity has the abstract QuantityKind it instantiates (e.g. 'wheelbase of robot X' —HAS_KIND→ 'length').
